clue.text: Support group essential for hiker?

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
a pack is a group, as of wolves or cub scouts

explanation.surface: Asks what holds up a walking club, or what a rambler cannot do without.
explanation.definitionFit: A rucksack carried on the shoulders is standard kit for anyone walking long distances, hence the question mark.

clue.text: I will leave European country for a period

indicators.note: the letter I leaves, so it is taken out of the country's name

parts.note: Spain is a country of Europe

explanation.surface: Someone announces they are emigrating from a European country for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: A span is a stretch of time, as in a lifespan or attention span.

clue.text: Information released linked to laws he abused in part of Australia

parts.note: news is information about events
something released is out, as a book or a prisoner

indicators.note: abused means misused or knocked about, so these letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A report is put out about some law that a man has twisted somewhere in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'linked to' is just glue; 'abused' scrambles LAWS HE to give the last six letters of the state's name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a state on the south-east coast of Australia, home to Sydney.

clue.text: He will love a greeting

parts.note: he will contracts to he'll
love is nil in tennis, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A man promises affection as a way of saying hi.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the commonest everyday word used to greet someone.

clue.text: Sea, true, is rough and harsh

indicators.note: rough suggests choppy, disordered water, so the letters are churned up

explanation.surface: A sailor grimly confirms that the sea is indeed rough and unforgiving.
explanation.definitionFit: Austere and harsh are synonyms, both describing severe, stern conditions or manner.

clue.text: Make improvements to attitude shown by salesman

indicators.note: the attitude belongs to and follows the salesman, so his letters come first

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
an air is a manner or attitude someone shows

explanation.surface: Advice on improving the manner a salesman shows to customers.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend or fix something is to make improvements to it.

clue.text: Perhaps remove blemishes from tyrant

parts.note: the prefix de- means to remove, as in de-ice
a spot is a blemish on the skin

explanation.surface: A beauty tip about clearing up spots, oddly applied to a dictator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' warns that DE-SPOT is an invented word meaning remove blemishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is an absolute ruler who wields power cruelly, the same as an autocrat.

clue.text: Queen tucks into elixir: a serving?

indicators.note: the queen's letter is tucked inside the elixir, as if eating it

parts.note: an elixir is a magic potion
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A monarch eagerly digs into a magic drink: is this a single helping?
explanation.definitionFit: A portion is one helping of food, the amount served to a person.

clue.text: Article caught on the radio dismissing Republican in the lead

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so the Republican's letter is removed

parts.note: something you caught on the radio is something you heard

explanation.surface: A news story heard on air about a Republican being fired by someone out in front.
explanation.walkthrough: No sound-alike here: 'caught on the radio' just means HEARD, which loses its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in front of the others, leading a race or contest, is being in the lead.

clue.text: Gallant, in quiet was going weak at the knees?

indicators.note: the word was goes inside the call for quiet

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
legs buckling are going weak at the knees

explanation.surface: A dashing hero, quietly overcome, goes weak at the knees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gallant' as an adjective is the definition; 'in' puts the clue's own word was inside the hush.
explanation.definitionFit: Swashbuckling describes a daring, flamboyant adventurer such as a pirate hero, which is gallant in a showy way.

clue.text: Swallows non-vegetarian foods, skipping starter

indicators.note: skipping the starter drops the first letter, as a diner skips the first course

parts.note: meats are foods vegetarians avoid

explanation.surface: A diner bolts down the meat dishes but skips the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skipping starter' takes M from the front of MEATS.
explanation.definitionFit: To swallow food is to eat it, so the third-person verbs match.

clue.text: Wild excitement erupting this year

indicators.note: erupting means bursting out violently, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A headline about frenzy breaking out over the past twelve months.
explanation.definitionFit: Hysteria is uncontrolled emotion or frenzied excitement, often in a crowd.

clue.text: Some bread given to church group

parts.note: a bun is a small bread roll

explanation.surface: Loaves are handed over to a congregation or parish group.
explanation.definitionFit: A bunch is a cluster or group of people or things, as in a bunch of friends.

clue.text: Flowering plant in border with cattle overhead

indicators.note: in a down answer the cattle sit above, so their letters come first

parts.note: cows are cattle
a lip is an edge or border, as of a cup

explanation.surface: A gardener describes a flower in a bed edged by a field of grazing cows.
explanation.definitionFit: The cowslip is a yellow-flowered wild primula of meadows.

clue.text: Leader at Plumpton damaged hoof in this exciting climax?

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
damaged means broken, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A racehorse at Plumpton injures its hoof in a thrilling finish.
explanation.walkthrough: Plumpton is a racecourse in Sussex. 'damaged' turns HOOF IN THIS into HOTOFINISH after the P.
explanation.definitionFit: A race so close that a camera picture decides the winner is a nail-biting climax.

clue.text: Soldier rolled over, sunk in better sleep

indicators.note: the reversed insect sinks into the word for better

parts.note: to cap is to better or outdo

indicators.note: rolled over means turned upside down, so the insect is read backwards

parts.note: a soldier ant is a kind of ant

explanation.surface: An infantryman has keeled over and nodded off, deep in a better bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' is not GI or TA here but the soldier ant; 'rolled over' turns it round and 'sunk in' buries it in a verb meaning outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: A catnap is a short sleep or doze, typically during the day.

clue.text: Sign of life you find in pod

definitions.meaning: a heartbeat felt at the wrist shows someone is alive
peas, beans and lentils are edible seeds grown in pods

explanation.surface: A doctor finding evidence of life inside an escape pod.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the heartbeat felt at the wrist and a legume seed such as lentils.

clue.text: New climb beginning

parts.note: an ascent is a climb

explanation.surface: A mountaineer setting out on a fresh route up a peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' tempts as the definition; it is only N.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent describes something just coming into being, starting to develop.

clue.text: Spider's first web at stake, fluttering in bin

indicators.note: fluttering means flapping about, so the letters are tossed into a new order
the first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A spider's web, strung on a garden stake, flaps in the wind beside the bin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fluttering' rearranges S (from 'Spider's first') with WEB AT STAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wastebasket is a container for rubbish, the same thing as a waste bin.

clue.text: One online comment, maybe, put in about witty reply

indicators.note: the number and the comment are placed inside the word for about

parts.note: re means about or concerning
I is the Roman numeral for one
a post is an online comment, for example on a forum

explanation.surface: Someone adds a single comment on the web about a clever comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, clever retort, originally a fencer's counter-thrust.

clue.text: First upsurge in sea at Calais entering jetty

indicators.note: the reversed sea goes into the jetty

parts.note: a pier is a jetty

indicators.note: in a down answer surging upward means read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: mer is French for sea, and Calais is a French port

explanation.surface: A wave surges up at the French port and over the harbour jetty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at Calais' asks for the French word; 'upsurge' reads it upward in this down clue, and 'entering' puts it into the jetty.
explanation.definitionFit: Premier means foremost or leading, as in the Premier League.

clue.text: Harm from deliberating on court case?

parts.note: someone deliberating on a trial is in, serving on, the panel
the jury is the panel that decides a court case

explanation.surface: Damage done by someone pondering a lawsuit.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words: a person deliberating on a court case is IN JURY.
explanation.definitionFit: Injury is damage or hurt, a synonym of harm as a noun.

clue.text: Run oven and cook meat, for example

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
an oast is a kiln or oven for drying hops

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions: switch the oven on and get the meat cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: An oast house is the cone-roofed kiln building where hops are dried in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast is to cook in the oven with dry heat, done to meat among other foods.

clue.text: Mother chasing pet in principle

indicators.note: chasing means following behind, so the mother's letters come after

parts.note: a dog is a common pet
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A mum runs after the family animal, at least in theory.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogma is a firmly held principle or doctrine laid down as true.
